description: Inverts the spectral envelope relative to the overall spectral envelope: energy associated with the highest frequency bands is transferred to the lowest and vice versa. It does NOT invert the frequencies themselves (see specnu slice mode 5 for that). Pinned to submode 1 (normal inversion); submode 2 additionally retains the source's amplitude envelope. Takes no parameters. Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: A parameterless timbral flip. Because the lowest partials of most sounds carry the greatest amplitude and the highest the least, swapping the envelope typically yields a much brighter timbre — or, depending on the source, one deeper and richer in character, as previously quiet regions become prominent. Derived from an idea by Allen Strange. A SPEC BARE pass (zeroing channels that don't contain harmonics) is built in, so distinctly pitched sources come out with a more 'harmonic' quality than amorphous ones. Worth feeding a range of material, from strong focused pitches to noisy textures — results vary widely with the source. If the result feels dynamically flattened, submode 2 keeps the original amplitude envelope for a closer-to-source version with just the timbral change.

examples.description: Invert the spectral envelope of a pitched source.
examples.expected_use: Brighten or hollow out a sound by exchanging the energy of its high and low bands.

known_issues: afta8's definitions carry a warning that 'at the time of last update, it has been found that this function is not working properly'. On this build it is mechanically sound: exit 0, deterministic, static duration, output non-silent (-13.6 dBFS vs -12.1 dBFS for the source round-trip) and distinct from submode 2's output. Whether the inversion is perceptually 'correct' on all material could not be adjudicated by probe; the warning is preserved here as advisory.
No numeric parameters exist, so there is nothing to breakpoint; the only choices are the submode and the source material.
